proof.text: Choose a local free generator using exists_isFreeGenerator and IsInvertible.sheafOfModules_isInvertible. Its germ gives a linear map from the stalk ring to the module stalk. It is surjective because every stalk element is represented on a smaller open, where the section is a unique multiple of the generator. It is injective because equality of germs holds after shrinking, where uniqueness of coefficients applies. Extend the resulting linear isomorphism to the residue field; the monoidal unit comparison identifies the result with the residue field, whose rank is one.

proof.text: The chosen tensorPullback adjunction and Mathlib pullbackPushforwardAdjunction have the same right adjoint. leftAdjointUniq identifies their left adjoints. Apply IsInvertible.pullback and transport invertibility by IsInvertible.of_iso.

proof.text: *(2), pullback of a tensor product.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal L$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal M$ there is an isomorphism $f^*(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)\cong f^*\mathcal L\otimes f^*\mathcal M$, natural in $\mathcal L,\mathcal M$, sending $f^*(s\otimes t)$ to $f^*s\otimes f^*t$.

Compose the chosen adjunctions af and ag, transport the right adjoint using pushforwardComp g f, and compare with the chosen adjunction for g ≫ f by leftAdjointUniq. Evaluate unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app on the open V and section s. The pushforward comparison is sectionwise identity, so this gives the stated composite section formula by definitional equality.

proof.text: Use braiding_hom_app_tmulSection for the symmetry formula. List.Perm induction gives the finite reordering isomorphism: nil is Iso.refl of the unit, cons tensors Iso.refl with the induction isomorphism, swap uses the inverse associator then braiding tensored with identity then associator, and trans composes isomorphisms. Equiv.Perm.ofFn_comp_perm supplies the list permutation, including n = 0.

source.place: Modules, Section 17.16 (Tag 01CA): symmetry and associativity of $\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}$

proof.text: Apply exists_tensorPullback_stalk_iso f x to obtain the stalk isomorphism e and germ formula. Map e.app L through extendScalars of X.residue x. Compose with the inverse of extendScalarsComp for f.stalkMap x then X.residue x, the equality transport from Scheme.residue_residueFieldMap, and extendScalarsComp for Y.residue (f x) then f.residueFieldMap x. ExtendScalars.map_tmul and the stalk germ formula compute the first map; extendScalarsComp_hom_app_one_tmul and the inverse identity compute the second; the equality transport is definitional on the pure tensor; the same composition lemma computes the last. The resulting value is 1 ⊗ residueValue s.

proof.text: Apply SheafOfModules.stalkTensorIso Y.toRingedSpace y, extend its comparison through F = extendScalars (Y.residue y).hom, and compose with the inverse monoidal tensorator μIso F. ExtendScalars.map_tmul reduces the value calculation to the supplied tensor-germ formula, expressed using tmulSection. extendScalars_δ_tmul then sends 1 ⊗ (s_y ⊗ t_y) to (1 ⊗ s_y) ⊗ (1 ⊗ t_y).
